Make TempleCBE Models Smaller With butcher

Source: R/butcher_methods.R
templecbe-butcher.Rd

Methods for [butcher::axe_call()], [butcher::axe_env()], [butcher::axe_data()] and [butcher::axe_rsample_data()] for [coxnet()] models, [cv_coxnet()] results and [joint_model()] fits, so that [butcher::butcher()] shrinks them as it does other models. They are used when butcher is installed, including on a parsnip fit or a fitted workflow with the `coxnet` engine.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'coxnet_model'
axe_call(x, verbose = FALSE, ...)

# S3 method for class 'coxnet_model'
axe_env(x, verbose = FALSE, ...)

# S3 method for class 'coxnet_model'
axe_data(x, verbose = FALSE, ...)

# S3 method for class 'cv_coxnet'
axe_call(x, verbose = FALSE, ...)

# S3 method for class 'cv_coxnet'
axe_env(x, verbose = FALSE, ...)

# S3 method for class 'cv_coxnet'
axe_data(x, verbose = FALSE, ...)

# S3 method for class 'cv_coxnet'
axe_rsample_data(x, verbose = FALSE, ...)

# S3 method for class 'joint_model'
axe_call(x, verbose = FALSE, ...)

# S3 method for class 'joint_model'
axe_env(x, verbose = FALSE, ...)

# S3 method for class 'joint_model'
axe_data(x, verbose = FALSE, ...)

Arguments

x

A `coxnet_model`, `cv_coxnet` or `joint_model`.

verbose

Passed to butcher: print the memory released.

...

Passed on to the methods of the inner objects.

Value

`x` with the parts above removed, with a `butchered_*` class added as butcher does.

Details

What each removes, and what still works afterwards:

* `axe_call()`: the call stored by glmnet (`print()` of the inner glmnet fit shows a placeholder). Predictions are unchanged. * `axe_env()`: the environments captured by the recipe steps of a recipe preprocessor (as butcher does for recipes) and, for a `joint_model`, the environment of its stored outcome formula, which is the frame the formula was written in (when that is a function's frame, saving the model saved every object in it). Predictions are unchanged. * `axe_data()`: for a `coxnet_model`, the training design matrix and outcome. Survival (`type = "survival"`) and restricted mean (`type = "time"`) predictions need the Breslow baseline hazard, which is computed from them; it is stored first at the model's default penalty, so predictions at that penalty are unchanged, and predictions at another penalty stop with an error. Linear predictors and `tidy()` work at any penalty. A model fit without a default penalty can then only predict linear predictors. For a `cv_coxnet` this applies to its refit model, whose default penalty is `lambda.min`; for a `joint_model`, to its Cox component, and the stored training data (`components$data`, `components$predictors`, `components$raw_predictors`) is removed too, so `predict()` and the explainers need `new_data` / `data` passed. * `axe_rsample_data()`: the `resamples` a `cv_coxnet` keeps, which hold the data once per resample when saved. Its metrics, `predict()`, `tidy()`, `collect_metrics()`, `autoplot()` and `print()` do not use them.

Examples

# \donttest{
if (requireNamespace("butcher", quietly = TRUE) &&
    requireNamespace("glmnet", quietly = TRUE)) {
  lung <- na.omit(survival::lung[, c("time", "status", "age", "sex", "ph.ecog")])
  fit <- coxnet(survival::Surv(time, status) ~ ., data = lung, penalty = 0.01)
  small <- butcher::butcher(fit)
  predict(small, lung[1:3, ], type = "survival", eval_time = c(100, 300))
}
#> # A tibble: 3 × 1
#>   .pred           
#>   <list>          
#> 1 <tibble [2 × 2]>
#> 2 <tibble [2 × 2]>
#> 3 <tibble [2 × 2]>
# }
